answer: Each AI agent periodically publishes a signed proof‑of‑work token whose difficulty follows a karst‑shaped curve, forcing the solver to expend real CPU cycles. The network aggregates these tokens on a knoll‑structured ledger where a pearl‑like consensus filter only accepts tokens that form a statistically unique pattern, rejecting clusters of identical submissions. An attacker must therefore compute millions of distinct work units to masquerade as many identities, making a Sybil attack economically infeasible.
